newsitem.title: FRANCE: France changes tone on Zaire rebels.
newsitem.headline: France changes tone on Zaire rebels.

text.p: France changed its tone on Thursday towards forces fighting to overthrow Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko, dropping the term "rebels" and referring to them for the first time by their chosen name.
The rebels, led by long-time opponent of Mobutu Laurent Kabila who have captured much of eastern Zaire, call themselves the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire.

French Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt made the subtle shift following a meeting in Lome, Togo on Wednesday between officials of Mobutu's government and Kabila's forces, which he called a positive step.
"The meeting yesterday, for the first time, of an official Zairean delegation and the AFDL is in itself a success that can be credited to the Lome summit," Rummelhardt said.
Officials said a high-level French delegation including President Jacques Chirac's Africa adviser, Michel Dupuch, was in Lome to promote the dialogue, alongside U.S. officials.
"The future of Zaire can only be conceived on the basis of democratic institutions created by free and fair elections," Rummelhardt added.
In only five months, the rebels have seized a quarter of the vast country, which Mobutu has ruled like an absolute monarch since 1965.

Zaire's ragged army has collapsed in the field and the key cities of Lubumbashi and Mbuji-Mayi, key to Zaire's vast mineral wealth of copper, cobalt, diamonds and precious metals, are now in rebel sights.
